subject: #373 Phase A coverage, driven live against the release binary
question: How many read-only operations actually reach `.passed` with `.semanticReadback` against live Logic today?

host.note: Logic WAS driven: the release binary was executed over stdio against the running Logic, one call plus one independent readback per registered operation.

reverify.expected: 21 of 23 read-only operations report passed/semanticReadback; tracks.list_library and tracks.scan_plugin_presets do not; all 90 mutating operations report notQualified/typedDeferral
reverify.cost: needs Logic running and `swift build -c release`; about a minute

method: Drive every registered operation through `QualificationTransport` against the real release binary and the running Logic, then histogram the results by mutability, status and verification kind rather than by whether the run as a whole passed.

observations.note: by design — the runner probes mutating operations with parameters that must be refused and asserts writeAttempted == false, so a qualification run cannot modify a project
list_library is the failure already pinned in knownLiveGateFailures; scan_plugin_presets needs a plug-in window, an environmental precondition

observations.what: what the roadmap said before this reading
what the static contract evaluator reports for the same tree
observations.reason: quoted from its own source — this static repo-tree evaluator has no live .passed data, and waivers.json holds zero entries, so every operation counts missing by construction

conclusion: Phase A is 21 of 23, live, today — not the 15 the roadmap carried, and not the zero the contract evaluator reports. The two that do not pass are both already understood: one is the pinned semantic mismatch and the other needs a plug-in window. So the remaining work for the read-only surface is not producing coverage; it is carrying coverage that already exists into the release evidence bundle and into a form the static evaluator can read. R-SEM's 113-of-113 measures the evaluator's blindness, not the product's.
limits: One run, one host, one project state, en-US. A different fixture could move `project.get_regions` or `tracks.scan_library`.
It says nothing about the 90 mutating operations, whose `.passed` branch deliberately does not exist; Phase B is unaffected by this reading.

`.passed` here is the transport's verdict on one call plus one independent readback. It is not the same as a release-grade evidence bundle, which additionally needs the raw transcript, the manifest entry and the signature.
The two failures were not re-diagnosed. They are quoted from their existing records rather than re-measured here.
